subject: Agriculture
title: Pheromone Traps
description: A micro-lesson that makes Pheromone Traps usable.

hook.text: Male moths follow female scent for miles. Synthetic pheromones exploit this drive to lure them into traps.

buildup.text: Pheromones are species-specific chemicals insects use to find mates. Scientists synthesize them in labs.

discovery.text: Traps baited with pheromones catch specific pest species without harming any other organisms. Zero collateral damage.

twist.text: Mating disruption floods orchards with pheromone so males can't find real females. Populations crash without a single kill.

climax.text: Pheromone-based control now protects most US apple orchards from codling moth—the industry's worst pest.

punchline.text: Confuse the males, crash the population. The gentlest pest control ever.

quiz.question: How does mating disruption with pheromones work?
options: Flooding the area with pheromone prevents males from finding real females
